processed_items.title: Parallel Worktree Campaign Orchestration (N worktrees + merge-orchestrator + quota tracking)
processed_items.note: NOVEL/IMPROVEMENT over existing skills. using-git-worktrees skill handles isolation per-agent (declarative isolation: worktree frontmatter v2.1.68+). dispatching-parallel-agents handles parallel dispatch. fan-out-scaling handles 3-phase scaling. The NEW piece is: (a) campaign-scoped slicing with explicit file boundaries to prevent overlap, (b) quota tracking across workers with redistribution, (c) merge-orchestrator that rebases all branches + resolves conflicts intelligently + runs full multi-tier build. Score breakdown: integration_complexity=50, token_efficiency=60, capability_expansion=75, maintenance=60, community_validation=70 = 63.25. Deferred (50-69 range): (1) the merge-orchestrator is the genuinely hard part and would need real-world validation, (2) campaign-style work is intermittent (38-post blog campaigns happen quarterly), (3) existing fan-out-scaling + using-git-worktrees probably cover 80% of value. Revisit if a future blog campaign or 20+ item audit explicitly stalls on sequential 8-wave fixes hitting quota limits.

processed_items.note: NOVEL — first novel item since prose-generation-claude-p-2026-05-31. Report cmd-3 (## Tooling Caveats): 'Distrust MCP responses that look truncated (20-char) — verify length and re-fetch or fall back to WebFetch/JSON APIs before building on them.' No prior digest entry across 12 weeks (grep 'distrust truncated'/'truncation detect' = 0). Score breakdown: integration_complexity=90, token_efficiency=55, capability_expansion=65, maintenance=90, community_validation=60 = 70.5. Distinct from maxResultSizeChars (server-side size-limit raise, not detection), mcp-doctor-skill (deferred diagnostic catalog), and the Circuit Breaker's reactive 2-attempt bail-out (assumes failure already noticed). This is the *detection* complement. Unlike sandbox/bwrap, MCP truncation NOT resolved by 2026-03-03 native-Linux migration — friction remains live (ChatGPT Pro 20-char, browser-MCP serializer).

processed_items.title: rsync-with-progress / chunked-verified transfers for large file copies (avoid silent cp stalls) (cmd-4)
processed_items.note: NOVEL but DEFERRED (50-69 range). Report cmd-4 (## Bash Conventions): 'For long Bash operations like large file copies, avoid commands that silently stall; use rsync with progress or chunked/verified transfers and report progress.' No prior digest entry. Score breakdown: integration_complexity=90, token_efficiency=50, capability_expansion=50, maintenance=90, community_validation=65 = 66.25. Deferred reason: narrow scope (large file copies), only 2 cited incidents (cp stalls during document saves), and the user now moves large data mostly via Syncthing + symlinks rather than manual cp. Consistent with prior narrow-Bash deferrals (json-helpers-lib 67.0, auto-format-hooks 64.5). Could be added as a one-line bullet to ## Shell/Bash Conventions if manual large-copy friction recurs.
